dropped_mechanisms.name: Alaska RHTP Tribal Health Technology Procurement Stack
dropped_mechanisms.detail: Fails Gates 3, 4, 5, and 7. Gate 7: The June 13 anatomization of the CMS Cooperative Agreement covered the same [CMS -> DOH -> tribal subgrants] layer chain. The 'tribal procurement authority' reframing does not survive source verification — the ANTHC EHR page (fetched) names the ANTHC BOARD as the decision body, not a single actor with independent procurement authority, and does not confirm Oracle Health as a selected vendor. Gate 3: Layer 2 (Hedberg subgrant decision authority) — the governor's appointment page establishes her as Commissioner but provides no specific RHTP subgrant approval authority. The ADN article (fetched, June 7, 2026) does not name Hedberg at all. The ANTHC EHR page directly contradicts the scout's claim that ANTHC has made an independent Oracle Health EHR decision — it shows only a board evaluation process with external consultant Impact Advisors. Gate 4: Neither the ADN article nor the govtech.com syndication (confirmed as a republication of the same Iris Samuels ADN piece) explicitly designates AI as an approved or priority use category for RHTP funds. The TAGGS award document describes 'technology integration' broadly, not AI specifically. Gate 5: No single named individual with a documented binary subgrant approval decision is confirmed. Hedberg's specific RHTP subgrant authority is not established by any fetched source. The ANTHC layer is an ANTHC Board — a committee, which explicitly fails Gate 5. All four gate failures are independent.

_validation_note: This is the ninth consecutive no-target cycle (June 12 through June 21, 2026). The 14-day window (June 7-21) was broadened to 21 days (May 31-June 21) per protocol, but the scouts surfaced no additional candidates in the May 31-June 6 extension window. Both candidates were dropped on multiple independent gate failures: Candidate A (DAF EUL RFLP) failed Gate 7 as a direct repeat of the June 10 anatomization. Candidate B (RHTP Tribal Procurement) failed Gates 3, 4, 5, and 7: the 'tribal procurement authority' reframing did not survive primary source verification (ANTHC EHR page confirmed board decision process, not independent single-actor authority; govtech article confirmed as syndication of same ADN piece, not independent source; Hedberg's RHTP-specific subgrant authority not established in any fetched document; AI is not explicitly designated as an approved use category in any program document). The bar was not lowered. An honest no-target is the correct outcome for this cycle.
